Definition: properly, a pithy maxim, usually of metaphorical nature; hence, a simile (as an adage, poem, discourse)
BiblicalUsage: mâshâl is a proverb, a pithy saying that carries truth in a picture. In 1 Kings 4:32 Solomon speaks three thousand proverbs, and in 1 Kings 9:7 Israel is warned she shall become a proverb and a byword among all people. In 1 Samuel 10:12 it becomes a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets, and in 1 Samuel 24:13 the proverb of the ancients says wickedness proceeds from the wicked. The word is wisdom that can be remembered.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mâshâl shows me that wisdom comes in short sentences that stay with me. I hold that Solomon's proverbs are God's gift to the ordinary day.
